excerpt: Compare short-term and long-term Dubai rental income after occupancy, operating costs, permits and management rather than headline revenue.
introduction:
A Dubai holiday home can generate a different pattern of revenue and expenses from an annual tenancy. A higher nightly gross amount does not necessarily mean more money for the owner after empty nights, cleaning, utilities, management and building charges. Compare both strategies over the same period using evidence for the actual apartment.

Holiday-home operation also requires the applicable Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism (DET) registration and permit. The worked example below compares the costs of the two rental strategies over the same period.
takeaways: Compare net income over the same year, including vacancy or occupancy and all owner-paid costs.
Check DET registration, the unit permit and building rules before operating a holiday home.
Test seasonality, operator fees and repairs; neither strategy guarantees a return.

sections.heading: Start with permitted use and the unit
sections.body:
DET's [holiday-home permit service](https://www.dubaidet.gov.ae/en/our-services/for-consumers-and-students/issue-a-new-holiday-homes-permit) describes applying for a residential unit to operate as a holiday home. Its [operator registration service](https://www.dubaidet.gov.ae/our-services/for-consumers-and-students/register-as-a-holiday-home-operator) explains registration through the Holiday Homes system. Confirm current eligibility, documents, fees, guest requirements and any operator licence with DET before listing or operating.

Check the building's rules and your mortgage, insurance and management agreement for the intended use. A residential unit and a long-term lease do not automatically establish that a holiday-home permit has been issued.

The [Business Bay and Dubai Marina investment guide](/journal/business-bay-vs-dubai-marina-rental-investment) provides area context, but the unit's permit and actual operating costs still need verification.

sections.heading: Calculate a sample year
sections.body:
Suppose a holiday home earns an average AED 650 per occupied night for 219 nights, equal to AED 142,350 of gross income. Assume cleaning AED 18,000, utilities AED 12,000, management AED 28,470, permit-related costs AED 3,500, building charges AED 16,000 and maintenance AED 8,000. These sample expenses total AED 85,970, leaving AED 56,380 before finance, tax and sale costs.

For the long-term alternative, assume AED 100,000 rent, AED 5,000 vacancy allowance and AED 27,500 of owner expenses, leaving AED 67,500 before finance, tax and sale costs. The chart shows the two results. All inputs are examples; actual occupancy, rates, fees and obligations vary.

This example excludes financing, initial furniture, replacement reserves and any pass-through guest levies. Add the items relevant to your own agreement and avoid counting a guest-paid levy as owner revenue.

chart.note: Sample assumptions; the comparison excludes financing, tax, initial furnishing and sale costs.

sections.heading: Build realistic short-term assumptions
sections.body:
Use comparable permitted properties with similar location, bedrooms, condition and amenities. Check whether displayed nightly prices are before platform charges, discounts or cleaning fees. Estimate occupied nights by season and allow for blocked dates, maintenance and gaps between bookings. A full calendar at the advertised rate is rarely a sound starting assumption.

Ask an operator for a written schedule of management and platform fees, cleaning, linen, utilities, maintenance, insurance and permit costs. Clarify whether percentages are charged on gross booking value or a different base and whether applicable tax is included.

Review the DET process for guest registration and reporting, and establish who is responsible. Confirm the permitted use and current requirements, and compare an operator’s revenue estimate with documented costs.

sections.heading: Build the long-term alternative
sections.body:
Use recent signed leases for similar units and record the lease term, furnishing, parking, included services and any rent-free period. Deduct a vacancy allowance, service charges, management, maintenance and insurance paid by the owner. The [Dubai net yield guide](/journal/how-to-calculate-net-rental-yield-in-dubai) explains how to compare the resulting income with total acquisition cost.

DLD's [tenancy registration service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/register-renew-ejari-contract/) describes registering or renewing a contract through Ejari. Confirm the current charges and each party's responsibilities under the actual agreement.

Include the cost of switching strategies, such as furnishing or removing furniture, and any downtime between tenancies. A long-term lease also has contractual notice and renewal terms.

sections.heading: Test a downside and the work involved
sections.body:
Recalculate the holiday-home case with fewer occupied nights, a lower realised rate and an urgent repair. Recalculate the long-term case with a longer void or non-payment and an additional repair. If a strategy only works under a full-occupancy assumption, review the investment and reserve.

Consider who responds to guests or tenants, arranges cleaning and repairs, maintains records and renews permits. A higher projected net income may require substantially more management time. Ask a licensed operator about service standards, reporting, repair authority and termination before signing.

Neither operating income figure includes the outstanding mortgage, personal tax position or eventual sale price. Prepare those separately for a full investment decision.

sections.heading: Estimate the occupancy needed to match the alternative
sections.body:
In the sample holiday-home example, suppose the AED 650 nightly income and 20% management charge remain unchanged, leaving AED 520 per occupied night before the other listed costs. If those other costs were fixed at AED 57,500, matching the long-term example's AED 67,500 would require about 241 occupied nights, or roughly 66% of a 365-day year. This break-even calculation shows how rental income and expenses interact.

In practice cleaning, utilities and other expenses can rise with occupancy, while rates can change by season and booking channel. Recalculate using your operator's actual fee basis and variable costs, and include any additional obligations. A break-even point based on unrealistic fixed costs will give false confidence.

sections.heading: Review a specific property
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Dubai project collection](/projects?emirate=Dubai) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with your property, budget and intended strategy. Ask for the building's current charges and the documents needed to assess permitted use.

Verify the holiday-home permit requirements with DET or the tenancy process with DLD, and use unit-specific evidence rather than the worked example.
